# MCUAPI

> Free, open, read-only REST API for the Marvel Cinematic Universe — movies, TV shows,
> characters, and the timeline connecting them across continuities. No API key required.

Base URL: https://mcuapi.up.railway.app/api/v1
OpenAPI spec: https://mcuapi.up.railway.app/docs/openapi.json
Interactive docs (Swagger UI): https://mcuapi.up.railway.app/docs
Health check: https://mcuapi.up.railway.app/health

## Key endpoints

- `GET /movies`, `GET /movies/{id}` — movies, filterable by `studio`/`continuity`/`multiverse_designation`/`is_mcu`
- `GET /tvshows`, `GET /tvshows/{id}` — TV shows, same filters as movies
- `GET /characters`, `GET /characters/{id}` — characters, plus `/characters/movie/{id}`, `/characters/tvshow/{id}`, `/characters/{id}/movies`, `/characters/{id}/tvshows`
- `GET /people`, `GET /people/{id}` — people (actors and directors) normalized out of the `played_by`/`directed_by` fields, plus `/people/{id}/characters` and `/people/{id}/titles`
- `GET /post-credit-scenes`, `GET /post-credit-scenes/{id}` — structured post- and mid-credits scenes, plus `/post-credit-scenes/movie/{id}` and `/post-credit-scenes/tvshow/{id}`
- `GET /timeline` — chronological ordering across continuities, independent of release date
- `GET /upcoming` — movies and TV shows with a future `release_date`, merged and sorted ascending
- `GET /titles` — movies and TV shows merged into one paged, filterable collection, joined in Postgres; unlike `/upcoming`, undated titles are included (sorted last)
- `GET /search?q=` — typo-tolerant search across movies, TV shows, characters (name and alias), and people, ranked by Postgres `pg_trgm` similarity; `?type=` narrows to one content type
- `GET /stats` — dataset-wide counts, including people and distinct continuities and multiverse designations

## Notes

- Every endpoint is a `GET`; the API never accepts writes.
- Rate limit: 100 requests/minute per IP.
- Responses include HAL-style `_links` for hypermedia navigation and are cacheable via `ETag`/`Cache-Control`.
- Full request/response schemas: see the OpenAPI spec above.
- A typed TypeScript client is published as `mcuapi-client` on npm.
- The whole dataset is also mirrored as static JSON on jsDelivr — see the README for URLs.
